transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Well, hi Dr. ____. What brings me in is... I guess I just feel like I’m always moving from one thing to the next, you know? Like I just can't idle. It's funny, actually, my brother is the exact same way. We used to rebuild old cars together back in the day, mostly Chevys, and he could never just sit and look at the engine, he always had a wrench in his hand, tweaking something. We found this beautiful '69 Chevelle once, rust bucket, but we got it running... Anyway, the new work setup at my job—I'm in customer service—has made this constant moving around a lot harder to hide. They changed the cubicles around and now everyone can see everything. It's a real pain, honestly.
Do you have trouble falling asleep?

Falling asleep? No, not really. I usually just hit the pillow and I'm out. Though, to be honest, half the time lately I end up falling asleep in my recliner. It's one of those big oversized leather ones, you know? I got it on sale at this furniture liquidation place a few years back. Best purchase I ever made. My wife hates it, she says it takes up way too much room in the den, but it used to have this really great massage feature. 

Well, the motor for it burned out a couple of months ago, actually. I flipped the whole chair over to try and fix it, but the wiring in those things is just a complete mess. It's not like the old Chevy engines where everything makes sense and you can actually trace the lines. I spent three hours just poking at the circuit board before I finally gave up... wait, what was the question? Oh, right, sleep. Yeah, no, my sleep is fine.
Do you find yourself falling asleep during the day when you don’t mean to?

During the day? No, no, I don't really doze off like that. I'm usually too keyed up anyway. Plus, at work, it's just back-to-back calls. You wouldn't believe how angry people get over a five-dollar late fee on their account. Just Tuesday, I had this guy yelling at me for twenty minutes straight because he forgot to mail his check. He kept blaming the post office, which, you know, fair enough, the post office around my neighborhood has been pretty terrible lately. 

My regular mail carrier, Frank, he's retiring next month, and the new guy filling in keeps putting my neighbor's mail in my box. They get these really high-end woodworking catalogs. Man, some of the lathes they sell in there are just incredible. I’ve always thought about getting into wood turning, making bowls or table legs, something like that. Seems like it would be a good way to keep my hands busy... but anyway, what did you ask? Oh, right, sleeping during the day. No, I stay awake just fine.
Do you often feel restless or have trouble sitting still?

Well, yeah, I do. Especially if I have to sit through something slow, like a training video at work or a long appointment. I start feeling real boxed in, you know? Like I just have to stand up, stretch my legs, or at least do something with my hands. 

It reminds me of this one training seminar they sent us to last year. Whole day thing at this hotel downtown. The chairs were those awful stacking banquet chairs, no padding at all. And the guy presenting, I swear he had the most monotone voice I’ve ever heard. He sounded exactly like my old high school history teacher, Mr. Henderson. Henderson used to just read straight from the textbook for an hour straight. I spent most of his class doodling in the margins of my notebook or taking my pen apart and putting it back together. I got so good at it I could reassemble a click pen blindfolded. Honestly, I think that's why I like fixing things so much, just figuring out how all the little pieces fit together. 

Anyway, during that seminar, I must have gotten up to get coffee like six times just to have an excuse to walk around. The coffee was terrible, too—tasted like burnt rubber. I ended up sneaking out at lunch and walking three blocks to find a decent diner. Found this great little place that made a killer pastrami on rye... wait, sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right, sitting still. Yeah, it's tough for me. I just get this urge to move.
Has this been causing problems for you at work, at home, or in relationships?

Work? Yeah, it's actually starting to become a bit of a problem there. My supervisors have been bringing it up in my recent reviews. They keep pointing out that I have all these unfinished tickets, or I make these little mistakes that end up slowing the whole team down. It's frustrating because I really am trying hard, and I usually get along great with the customers. 

Like I was saying before about that guy with the late fee, I actually managed to calm him down eventually. We ended up talking about his grandson's little league team for a good ten minutes. I used to coach little league, you know, back when my son was younger. We had this one kid on the team, Tommy, who couldn't hit a ball to save his life, but man, he could run like the wind. Once he got on base, it was a guaranteed run. We made it all the way to the regional championships that year. We played this team from two towns over, and they had uniforms that looked just like the Oakland A's. I always liked those colors, the green and gold. Reminds me of this old jacket I used to have... wait, what was the question? Oh, right, problems. Yeah, at work it's definitely showing up in my reviews with the unfinished tickets and all that.
Did these attention and focus problems start when you were a child?

Childhood? Yeah, actually. Looking back, this was around long before this job change. I know because my mom used to keep all my old report cards in this big cedar chest at the foot of her bed. Man, I love the smell of cedar. I actually bought a bunch of cedar blocks for my own closet a couple of months ago because I found a moth hole in my favorite wool sweater. It was this really nice navy blue cardigan, super warm. I tried to patch the hole myself, but my sewing skills are pretty much nonexistent. I ended up making this huge, lumpy knot on the sleeve, and my wife just took one look at it and laughed. I think she ended up donating it. I always wonder if whoever bought it at the thrift store managed to fix the sleeve or if they just wear it lumpy. 

But anyway... what was I saying? Oh, right, the report cards in the chest. Yeah, I was looking through them a while back, and in grade school, pretty much all my teachers wrote the exact same thing in the comments section. They'd say that I was bright but careless, that I always talked out of turn, and that I constantly had to be reminded to stay with my work. So yeah, I guess I've been like this since I was a little kid.
